newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds suffer pain with T-bonds, but seen recoverin.
newsitem.headline: Bunds suffer pain with T-bonds, but seen recoverin.

text.p: German debt prices were knocked off their pedestal late on Wednesday as stronger than expected U.S. industry output data sent U.S. Treasuries skidding down.
The late afternoon weakness wiped away all the morning's progress, but analysts said the market was still in good enough shape to trade higher again in the next few sessions.
"The German market is just being pushed and pulled by the U.S. at the moment," said one trader in London. "On its own, it looks quite happy."

By 1415 GMT, the DTB June Bund futures was 21 basis points lower on the day at 100.60. The contract earlier inched up to 101.01, but lacked the nerve to remain above the key 101.00 resistance level, and quickly retreated.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was priced at 101.04 by 1419 GMT, offering a 5.874 percent yield.
Analysts said the German market would use downward pull of the U.S. as a chance to consolidate on Tuesday's hefty gains, but would soon be ready to pick itself up again.
Martin Siegert, derivatives portfolio manager at LandesgiroKasse in Stuttgart, said the 100.42/45 would be a good base for the June future to head for at first.
"We think 100.45 will be good support, but after that we are looking for a test of 100.02," he said.
But in the next few sessions, Siegert said the futures contract could tackle key technical retracement targets at 101.15 and 101.19.
Despite Bunds' late retreat, the cash market significantly outpaced its U.S. counterpart over Wednesday's session, bloated the 10-year yield gap to 121 basis points by 1436 GMT.
